evidence.excerpt: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of EMC problems specific to low-voltage distribution systems, intended for practising engineers and postgraduate students. The presentation proceeds from the physical mechanisms of conducted disturbance generation in power electronic equipment through to network propagation, coupling to sensitive loads, and measurement practice. The regulatory framework covering CISPR 11, CISPR 32, IEC 61000-3-2, IEC 61000-3-12 and EN 50160 is described with attention to applicability conditions and current revision status as of 2020. Frequency-domain and time-domain modelling approaches are compared for three representative scenarios: aggregated residential loading, industrial bus with variable-speed drives, and mixed-use low-voltage feeders with embedded generation. Common measurement pitfalls including grounding, LISN placement, and ambient noise subtraction are discussed with illustrative examples drawn from the authors' laboratory experience. The chapter concludes with an outline of open research questions including the standardisation of supraharmonic measurement methods and probabilistic compliance assessment.
